# PreFlight Audit Tool

> A free, in-browser static security audit for apps built with AI coding tools (Lovable, Cursor, Bolt, Replit, Claude Code) and any other web application. 117 probes covering OWASP Top 10 2025 (A01-A10) and OWASP LLM Top 10 2026 (LLM01, LLM02, LLM03, LLM08, LLM09, LLM10), plus 2025–2026 supply-chain incidents (including the May 11, 2026 Mini Shai-Hulud TanStack worm), MCP security, AI-tooling rules-file backdoors, post-infection IOC detection, AST-based code-correctness checks, multi-language adapters (Python, Go, Ruby, PHP, Java, Kotlin, Swift, Scala, Elixir, Dart, C#, Rust), and conventional SAST checks. Every finding carries the OWASP category code(s) it maps to. All scanning runs locally in the browser — no upload, no signup, no analytics beacons.

The PreFlight Audit Tool is published by Mid-Atlantic AI (https://midatlantic.ai). Contact: John@midatlantic.ai. License: free for individual and team use.

## Key pages

- [PreFlight, the tool](https://preflight.midatlantic.ai/): run a free security scan of an AI-built app in the browser, no signup.
- [Learn](https://preflight.midatlantic.ai/learn/): guidance on building AI-generated apps safely.
- [Field reports](https://preflight.midatlantic.ai/learn/incidents/): plain-language write-ups of real supply-chain and AI-tooling incidents, verified against primary sources.
- [OWASP LLM Top 10, 2025 to 2026 shift](https://preflight.midatlantic.ai/owasp-llm-2026/): how the LLM Top 10 reordered toward agent risk.
- [OWASP Agentic Top 10](https://preflight.midatlantic.ai/owasp-agentic-2026/): the ASI01 to ASI10 risks specific to AI agents.
- [OWASP coverage](https://preflight.midatlantic.ai/learn/owasp/): which OWASP categories each probe maps to.
- [Privacy contract](https://preflight.midatlantic.ai/privacy/): why nothing leaves the browser.

## What it does

The tool extracts text from selected files or a public GitHub repository and runs 117 pure-function probes against the content. Each probe emits zero or more findings with severity (critical / high / medium / low / info), a CWE reference, a file path and line number, evidence, and a remediation block. Findings are aggregated into a risk score out of 100 with a tier label (LOW / MODERATE / HIGH / CRITICAL RISK), and broken out into four area scores: security, code health, accessibility, and discoverability. The headline score reflects security exposure only. Code-health, accessibility and discoverability findings are reported in full and shown on their own axis, but do not reduce it, because a security number dragged down by opinions about function shape or a missing meta tag is answering the wrong question. An area with no findings reads "clear" rather than 100, since a perfect score and an area that never applied are different claims. The tier label is additionally clamped to the worst real finding: a project with no critical and no high findings is never labelled HIGH or CRITICAL no matter how many cosmetic findings it carries.

## Input modes

- **GitHub URL** — paste `https://github.com/owner/repo`; the tool reads up to 80 security-relevant files via the unauthenticated GitHub API (60-requests-per-hour-per-IP limit).
- **Files / Folder** — select files or a directory via the browser File API; contents are read with `FileReader.text()` and never leave the tab.

## Output

- Interactive results dashboard with score gauge, severity distribution, category breakdown, expandable findings with ±5-line code snapshots.
- Five export formats: JSON (machine-readable schema `midatlantic-audit/v1`), Markdown report, GitHub PR-comment Markdown (collapsible `<details>` block), agent-ready fix-this prompt (formatted for Claude / ChatGPT / Cursor), single-snippet copy.
- Local scan history (up to 10 entries, localStorage-only) with one-click View (load cached findings) or Re-run (re-fetch + re-scan).
- Baseline diff vs. prior scan of the same source (introduced / fixed / persisted findings, score delta).
- Diagnostics drawer with structured logs (debug / info / warn / error filterable, copy / save / clear).

## The 117 probes

Two groups:

1. **Core probes** (51, items 1-51). JavaScript / TypeScript / Python / SQL / config-file analysis, AI-tooling and supply-chain checks, plus two dataflow probes (intra-file and cross-file taint). Run regardless of language.
2. **Multi-language adapters** (66, items 52-117). Per-language coverage of the cross-language failure shapes (Unsafe / Untrusted Deserialization, Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret) plus XL-013 JWT signature verification. Every one of the 15 languages now ships the JWT check. Languages: Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Go, Java, C, C++, C#, Kotlin, Swift, Ruby, PHP, Scala, Elixir, Dart.

In registry order (matches `src/lib/probes.js` PROBES array):

1. **Architecture** — classifies project shape and emits informational findings tailored to it.
2. **Secret Scanner** — provider API keys (AWS, Stripe, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, GitHub, Slack, and more), generic hardcoded secrets, DB connection URLs with credentials, private key blocks.
3. **NEXT_PUBLIC_ Misuse** — server secrets exposed via the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` client-bundle prefix.
4. **Supabase RLS** — tables without row-level security enabled; permissive `USING (true)` policies.
5. **Firebase Rules** — `allow read/write: if true`, rules granting any authenticated user full access.
6. **Package.json** — suspicious postinstall hooks, non-registry dependencies, floating versions.
7. **Env File Hygiene** — `.env` files tracked in the repo.
8. **Auth Weakness** — JWT `algorithm: none`, `jwt.verify` without a secret, `eval`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Comment-aware.
9. **Python Security** — Python-specific dangerous patterns (shell injection, unsafe YAML, weak hashing in a credential context).
10. **Weak Cryptography** — MD5/SHA1 for credentials, static IVs, missing KDF parameters, weak cipher modes.
11. **Admin Route Exposure** — admin surfaces gated only by client-side auth hooks.
12. **Security Headers** — missing security response headers in `next.config` / host config.
13. **CORS** — wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.
14. **LLM Security** (OWASP LLM Top 10 2026) — prompt injection, LLM calls from client code (key exposure), LLM output rendered as HTML, dangerous agent tools, destructively-named tools, system prompts in client bundles, unbounded `max_tokens`.
15. **Webhook Validation** — Stripe / GitHub webhooks without signature verification.
16. **GitHub Actions** — `pull_request_target` checking out untrusted code, actions pinned to mutable refs.
17. **Client Auth Storage** — auth tokens in `localStorage`.
18. **SSRF / Open Redirect** — redirect targets and server-side fetches driven by user input.
19. **Cookie Security** — auth cookies missing `httpOnly` / `secure` / `sameSite`.
20. **API Route Auth** — sensitive / destructive API routes with no auth check.
21. **Compromised Packages** — known-malicious dependency versions from 2025-2026 supply-chain incidents, by exact version.
22. **Slopsquat / Typosquat** — typosquatted and LLM-hallucinated package names.
23. **MCP Security** — MCP servers spawning shell interpreters, `mcp-server-git` pre-Dec-2025, servers bound to 0.0.0.0.
24. **Trojan Source** — bidirectional-control-character Unicode attacks in source.
25. **AI Rules Files** — `.cursorrules` / `.cursor/rules` / `.windsurfrules` / `CLAUDE.md` with bidi control chars or instruction-override phrasing.
26. **Malicious Artifacts** — post-infection indicators of compromise dropped on disk by known worms.
27. **Agent Config Backdoor** — `.claude/settings*.json` hooks on auto-firing events, `.vscode/tasks.json` tasks with `runOn: folderOpen`.
28. **AI Code Smells** — the tells of code generated and shipped without a read-through.
29. **URL Reputation** — raw IPs, shorteners, suspicious TLDs, HTTP-only hosts in source.
30. **HTML Hygiene** — unsafe HTML patterns and missing hardening attributes.
31. **Reflected XSS** — user input reaching the DOM without escaping.
32. **SEO Hygiene** — discoverability metadata (informational, does not affect the security score).
33. **GEO Hygiene** — generative-engine-optimization metadata (informational).
34. **A11y Landmarks** — accessibility landmark checks (informational).
35. **Code Quality** — maintainability and error-handling hygiene (health axis).
36. **Code Correctness** — AST-based scope-validity checks (undeclared identifiers).
37. **Package Manager Hardening** — lockfile / install-script hardening advice.
38. **SQL Injection** — string-interpolated SQL in JavaScript / TypeScript.
39. **Path Traversal** — user input reaching filesystem paths.
40. **Weak Randomness** — `Math.random` used for security-bearing values.
41. **Stack Trace Leaks** — stack traces returned to clients.
42. **Subresource Integrity** — third-party scripts without SRI.
43. **Source Map Exposure** — source maps shipped to production.
44. **Iframe Sandbox** — iframes without a restrictive `sandbox` attribute.
45. **Security Logging** — auth events with no logging hooks.
46. **RAG Ingestion** — user-supplied content ingested into a vector store without provenance.
47. **Vector Embedding Weaknesses** — vector search without a per-tenant scope filter.
48. **Taint Flow** — intra-file dataflow from a user-input source to a dangerous sink (AST-based).
49. **Cross-File Taint** — a source in one file reaching a sink in another through an imported function (function-summary dataflow).
50. **Host Detection** — attributes which AI build tool produced the repo (classifier, informational).
51. **AI Codegen Bloat** — the tells of un-read AI-generated code (maintainability, informational).

### Multi-language adapters (52-117)

Every language ships some combination of Unsafe / Untrusted Deserialization, Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, and XL-013 JWT Signature Verification. All 15 languages now carry the JWT check.

- **Python** — Unsafe Deserialization, Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **JavaScript / TypeScript** — TLS Verification Disabled (the SQL, secret, and auth shapes for JS/TS are covered by the core probes above).
- **Rust** — Untrusted Deserialization, Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **Go** — Untrusted Deserialization, Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **Java** — Unsafe Deserialization, Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **C** — Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **C++** — Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **C#** — Unsafe Deserialization, Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Token Validation Disabled.
- **Kotlin** — Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **Swift** — Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **Ruby** — Unsafe Deserialization, Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **PHP** — Unsafe Deserialization, Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **Scala** — Unsafe Deserialization, Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **Elixir** — Unsafe Deserialization, Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **Dart** — Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret, JWT Signature Not Verified.
- **Dart** (94-96): Raw SQL Interpolation, TLS Verification Disabled, Hardcoded Secret.

## What it does NOT do

- No live exploitation. We are static analysis. We say "this looks bad"; we do not run payloads.
- No IDOR / BOLA testing — those require a running auth context.
- No runtime probing of deployed endpoints.
- No back-end. There is no server. The tool is a single-page React app.
- No data collection beyond local-only counter analytics (counts of `scan_started`, `probe_run.<name>`, `export.<format>`, etc.; never URLs, file content, or finding details).

## Differentiators from other security tools

- **Free, no signup, no credit card.** Open the page; scan; done.
- **Privacy by architecture, not by promise.** Everything runs in the browser. There is no server that could leak data.
- **AI-tooling-specific probes in the free tier.** MCP attack surface, Cursor / Copilot rules-file backdoors, slopsquatted package names, system prompts leaked to client bundles, prompt-injection sinks.
- **2025–2026 threat intel hard-coded.** Specific versions from named incidents, not generic CVE matching.
- **Agent-friendly exports.** "Copy Agent Prompt" formats findings for Claude / ChatGPT / Cursor with code snippets and explicit fix-this framing.
- **Pre-merge gate.** A single browser-tab scan you can run before committing — focused on failure modes specific to AI-generated code (Cursor/Copilot rules-file backdoors, MCP misconfig, slopsquatted packages, prompt-injection sinks).

## Architecture

Single-page React 18 application, Vite-built, react-router-dom v6 for routing, no backend. `App.jsx` (~950 lines) orchestrates state; the probe registry lives in `src/lib/probes.js` and aggregates 117 pure-function probes across dedicated modules: v0.4 baseline probes in-file, AST-based Code Correctness probe under `src/lib/probes/code-correctness.js`, v0.5 OWASP-framed additions under `src/lib/probes/v05.js` + `v05b.js`, and the per-language adapters under `src/lib/probes/v05-phase3-*`. Learn content lives under `src/learn/{patterns,incidents,shapes}/*.md` (YAML frontmatter + Markdown body, parsed at runtime). 4,027 tests across 116 files covering probes, formatters, history, scoring, snippet rendering, logger behavior, Learn content shape, suppression workflow, .preflight.yml schema, the AST probe, and the v0.5 adversarial / false-positive suite per language.

Stack:
- React 18 + Vite 5
- lucide-react for icons
- localStorage for history and analytics
- Vitest + jsdom for tests
- No remote services, no external API keys, no fetch destinations other than `api.github.com` and `raw.githubusercontent.com` (only when scanning a GitHub URL the user explicitly entered)

## Accessibility

- WCAG 2.1 AA compliant color contrast (verified pair-by-pair against the brand palette).
- Full keyboard navigation. Skip-to-content link. Focus-visible outlines.
- ARIA combobox / listbox on the URL autocomplete dropdown.
- ARIA dialog with focus trap on the Diagnostics drawer.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` honored.
- All findings communicated by both color AND text label (no color-only signal).
- Screen reader tested with NVDA.

## Versioning + freshness

- Schema version: `midatlantic-audit/v1` (JSON export).
- Probe set last expanded: 2026-08-27 (XL-013 JWT signature verification completed across all 15 languages, cross-file taint analysis added).
- Threat intel last updated: 2026-05-12 (Mini Shai-Hulud TanStack "TheBeautifulSandsOfTime" campaign by TeamPCP — 170+ packages across @tanstack, @mistralai, @opensearch-project, @uipath, @squawk, and unscoped victims).
- Brand: Mid-Atlantic AI — palette navy `#0a1226` / orange `#f26b1f` / mint `#9fe5dd`.
